quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass a car going the same direction.
Only during the day.
Anytime.
When turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how long it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on three things: perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
A roundabout is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn the direction the arrow points.
These lanes are for buses and vehicles with multiple passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your vehicle slides on water between the tires and the road. Worn tires, low air pressure, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Traffic lights sometimes show arrows for turns from certain lanes. What does a green arrow mean?

options.text: It is only used on one-way streets.
It means proceed, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may only proceed if a green arrow and a circular green light both appear.
It points to the nearest airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means proceed, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go, but traffic in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights
Low beam headlights
High beam headlights
It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: A load extending more than ____ beyond the rear of a vehicle must have a red flag during the day.

options.text: One foot
Two feet
Three feet
Four feet

questions.correctAnswerText: Four feet
questions.explanation: If a load extends more than four feet past the rear of your vehicle, it must have a red flag during daylight in clear weather. The flag should be 18 inches square. At night or in poor visibility, use red lights and reflectors.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is about to appear. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When driving on highways, you should:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep scanning with your eyes.
Be ready to respond to hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready to react to unexpected dangers. Scan your surroundings to avoid highway hypnosis by not looking at one spot too long.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
All around your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: All around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space all around your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on either side.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by releasing the accelerator. When moving very slowly, apply the brakes lightly and move off the road to a safe area.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must focus completely on driving. Doing any other task while driving is dangerous. Drivers make many decisions every mile, so full attention is necessary.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is clear to do so.

questions.question: A solid white line on the road's right edge slants toward the left. This means:

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You must turn left just ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid edge line marks where the road ends. When the line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful where children play. Children may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop ahead.
Buggy warning.
Limited parking.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming. Be ready to stop completely before going forward.

questions.question: When you see this sign, it means:

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. In this case, the road curves to the left. Multiple chevron signs mark the curve.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal a lane change.
Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Also check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Copy what other cars are doing instead of following the guard.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from a crossing guard, sign, or law enforcement officer. Drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way stop sign intersection. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, yield to the driver on your right. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What best keeps you and others safe when you back up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before putting the car in reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you sit in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio before backing up to alert people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you sit in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is hard because drivers cannot see well behind their vehicles. Before you get in the car to back up, walk to the back and check for children and small objects.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are sitting in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have any open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road or sidewalk. You cannot have an open alcohol container in any seat of a motor vehicle on a public road.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of having an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect how well you drive. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your concentration. It is better to wait until you feel calm before driving.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before you turn on your engine.
While backing out of your driveway.
When you are going 55 mph.
When you finish a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you turn on your engine.
questions.explanation: Before you drive, check that all your equipment works. Before you start the engine, adjust all mirrors so you can see without leaning forward or backward.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive normally since their emotions do not affect driving.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Take time to calm down before starting the engine.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take time to calm down before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: If you are worried, excited, crying, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Emotions distract you because your mind is on something else. Calm down and get focused before you drive.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that you cannot see in side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What is the rule about posters, signs, and stickers on windshields and windows?

options.text: They are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.
They are allowed if the driver can still see.
They are not allowed unless the law requires them.
They are allowed if they do not have bad language.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not allowed unless the law requires them.
questions.explanation: You cannot put anything on your vehicle's windows. No signs, posters, or stickers can be on a window unless the law says they must be there.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when can you pass?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
Only on an expressway.
If there is no oncoming traffic.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is no oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line in the middle of the road with the broken line on your side, you may cross to pass if no cars are coming toward you.

questions.question: What color lines separate lanes moving in the same direction?

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Solid white lines separate lanes going in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines separate lanes going the same way and can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate lanes going in opposite directions.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers and pedestrians when they may not see you. If you think another driver will hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left curve is ahead.
A series of curves is ahead.
An S-curve is ahead.
The road will be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will be slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is especially slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: You are driving in another driver's blind spot. What should you do?

options.text: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: What can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allowing extra travel time.
Obeying posted speed limits.
Using proper turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a specific number of occupants.
Specific turning movements are allowed from specific lanes.
Do not enter.
Drivers in both lanes are responsible for merging smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a specific number of occupants.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. HOV lanes are reserved for buses and vehicles with a driver and one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed where the sign is posted.

questions.question: A green arrow changes to a solid green light. What should you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
You must go straight and cannot turn.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the arrow's direction but must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Before you start the car, what should you check?

options.text: That backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
That adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
That child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
That all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: That all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before you start the engine, make sure you and all passengers have buckled your seat belts.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Your current road ends ahead.
You must bear either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection is ahead. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: How should you adjust your seat belt?

options.text: Loose.
Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Hidden beneath the seat.
So the buzzer or light stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: Lap belts should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. Shoulder belts should be comfortable enough for you to fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should:

options.text: Be on high beam.
Be on low beam.
Be off. Use parking lights instead.
Be on high beam or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be on low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when another vehicle is coming toward you or ahead of you. Switch to low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other cars.
Drive slower than other cars.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars around them. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, within the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
Stop completely and let others go first.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others go first if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others go first if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down at the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread.
Keep your tires at the right pressure.
Drive slower when it rains.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires with good tread and at the right pressure. Drive slower when it rains. Hydroplaning happens most often when driving fast in wet conditions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass carefully.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is coming. The road splits into two separate one-way roads with a divider between them. Stay on the right side.

questions.question: When can you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your car. This warns other drivers of danger.

questions.question: To pass a slower car on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the center line.
Flash your lights at oncoming cars.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic to complete your pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
Stop immediately and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
Drive faster to get out of the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They show that work is happening on or near the road. Drive with extra care when you see these signs.

questions.question: When passing on a highway with multiple lanes:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What colors are signs that show the distance to the next highway exit?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Signs that give information about destinations are green with white letters or pictures.
